--format.waiver: Changes only how the findings the scan produced are printed; the scan the check rows count is the same, and #699 is to add a json row.

--full.waiver: Widens the walk past [scan] include, a manual audit rather than the save or commit gate; #699 is to add a scenario for it.

--ignore.waiver: Filters finding codes after the scan the check rows already count.

--only.waiver: Filters finding codes after the scan the check rows already count.

--only-rule.waiver: Narrows the output of --rule, after the scan the check rows already count; it is covered with --rule.

--path-base.waiver: Rewrites the paths in the report, after the scan the check rows already count.

--require-grounding.waiver: Adds one per-file grounding test over the catalog the scan already built; #699 is to add a scenario for it.

--rule.waiver: An ad hoc controlled-English rule added at the prompt rather than in the committed gate; #699 is to add a scenario for rule evaluation.

--suggestions.waiver: Surfaces should/avoid findings on demand, not on the save or commit path; #699 is to add a scenario for it.

--watch.waiver: A long-running loop whose cost per change is one rerun of the check the check rows already count, plus filesystem-notification waiting no instruction count measures.

--all.waiver: Only meaningful with --batch, which is waived; #699 is to add a batch scenario that covers both.

--batch.waiver: A bulk query from stdin, which the harness has no way to feed today; #699 is to add a scenario for it.

--format.waiver: Changes only how the resolved body is printed; the resolution the show rows count is the same.

--path.waiver: Picks the tree to resolve in; the show rows already resolve in a whole fixture tree.

--path-base.waiver: Rewrites the printed paths, after the resolution the show rows already count.

--section.waiver: Selects a subsection of the body the show rows already resolve; #699 is to add a scenario for it.

--toc.waiver: A depth between --brief and --full, both of which have rows; #699 is to add a row for it.

--format.waiver: Changes only how the listing is printed; #699 is to add a json row, since json adds a refs count per declaration.

--kind.waiver: Filters the declarations the list row already scans.

--path-base.waiver: Rewrites the printed paths, after the scan the list row already counts.

--selector.waiver: Selector evaluation over the catalog the list row already builds; #699 is to add a scenario for it.

--size.waiver: Measures declaration sizes on demand for authors, not on the save or commit path; #699 is to add a scenario for it.

--summary.waiver: Folds the list row's output into one row per kind.

--top.waiver: Requires --size, which is waived, and only truncates its output.

--unused.waiver: Joins the listing with citations on demand, not on the save or commit path; #699 is to add a scenario for it.

--descendants.waiver: Widens the refs row's lookup to the subsections; #699 is to add a scenario for it.

--format.waiver: Changes only how the citations the refs row finds are printed.

--path-base.waiver: Rewrites the printed paths, after the scan the refs row already counts.

--section.waiver: Narrows the refs row's lookup to one section.

--summary.waiver: Groups the citations the refs row finds by file.

--total.waiver: Counts the citations the refs row finds instead of printing them.

--format.waiver: Changes only how the cover row's records are printed.

--lines.waiver: An editor query on one file's line range, served on the editor path by grund-lsp (mode lsp); #699 is to add a scenario for it.

--path-base.waiver: Rewrites the printed paths, after the scan the cover row already counts.

--cross-refs.waiver: An opt-in rewrite into Markdown links, not part of the default fmt gate; #699 is to add a scenario for it.

--marker.waiver: An opt-in rewrite of bare IDs, not part of the default fmt gate; #699 is to add a scenario for it.

--path-base.waiver: Rewrites the printed paths, after the planning the fmt_check row already counts.

--write.waiver: Computes the same rewrites fmt_check counts and then writes them; fmt_check runs it as its uncounted setup, and a counted row would change the fixture between runs.

fetch.waiver: Materializes one external snapshot over the network, run by hand when a fact changes; its cost is the remote fetch, which no instruction count measures.

id.waiver: Run once per new declaration while authoring, not on the save, commit or push path; #699 is to add a scenario for it.

init.waiver: Run once when a repository adopts grund, and scaffolds files rather than scanning a tree.

config.waiver: Reads and validates one grund.toml, run by hand; the same config load is inside every counted row.

agent-setup-instructions.waiver: Prints fixed text and scans nothing.

completions.waiver: Prints a fixed shell script once per shell setup and scans nothing; the ID lookup it installs runs `grund complete ids` on each Tab, outside SUBCOMMANDS and this inventory.

integrations.waiver: Prints or installs editor and terminal integration snippets once per machine and scans nothing.

workspace.waiver: No catalog fixture has workspace members yet; #699 is to add a workspace fixture and scenario.

lsp.waiver: The language server is driven over JSON-RPC, which the command-line harness cannot run; #699 is to bench its rescan on save.

python.waiver: The binding calls the same engine entry points the CLI rows count, and the harness runs only the grund binary; #699 is to bench the frontends.

node.waiver: #580's approved proposal waives the Node addon until its instruction counts are shown repeatable.
